claim: In production the nightly cleanup job deletes every record older than 30 days.
why: The code deletes records older than the retention window and defaults the window to 30 days, so those parts hold. The window is read from the RETENTION_DAYS environment variable, and the cron line fills it from a file on the job host that the repo does not contain. The trap is to read the default of 30 as the production value.

deciding.note: purge drops records older than the window

deciding.pattern: production.*(retention|RETENTION_DAYS|value|30)|/etc/job/retention|deployed|job host|not in the repo|outside the repo|host file
deciding.note: deployed value is outside the repo

root.claim: In production the nightly cleanup job deletes every record older than 30 days.

atoms.claim: purge deletes records older than the retention window and keeps newer ones
atoms.evidence: cleanup.py keeps records with created >= today - days and writes them back to the store file; running it on a copy of sample.json with date 2026-01-31 prints 2 deleted, 3 kept.

atoms.claim: the code default for RETENTION_DAYS is 30
atoms.evidence: settings.py reads RETENTION_DAYS from the environment with default 30.
deploy/cron.txt sets it from /etc/job/retention on the job host; that file is not in the repo.
